context.text: Accurate predictions can coexist with disputes about explanation and ontology. The essays take positions within those disputes.

opening: Physics can predict an experiment exquisitely while leaving physicists arguing about what exists. The contributors to this collection take those arguments seriously: how quantum theory relates to gravity, what probability means, and whether apparently distant events require mysterious connections. These are researchers explaining problems they work on, including proposals that remain open to dispute. Reading across the essays brings the unsettled foundations into view, where getting the calculations right does not remove the need to say what kind of world could produce them.
